brief: announce() assigns tickerEl.textContent outright (~line 534), so two events in the same frame show only the second — the town's one text surface silently drops lines and has done since it was built. That is also what blocks c4: the church-answer branch in strikeClock (~line 3143) is unreachable dead code, because `(hInt === 9 || hInt === 18)` hangs off an else-if under `(hInt % 3 === 0)` and both 9 and 18 are divisible by three; it cannot simply be un-nested while a second announce in the same frame would erase the first. Fix the cause, then the symptom: make announce() a small ordered queue with a minimum dwell per line, and then let the church actually answer the clock at nine and eighteen.
successLooksLike: At nine o'clock on day 2 or later you read the clock line and then the church line, in that order, both legible; no line is ever cut off mid-word by another.
avoid: Do not grow the ticker into a log or a second UI element — it is one line and should stay one line. Do not let the queue back up; drop stale entries rather than showing an old line late.
